The known results in the plane state that a polynomial map \(F=(p,q):\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}^2\) with a nowhere‑zero Jacobian determinant is guaranteed to be globally injective whenever one of its components has degree at most 2; this is sharp, since counter‑examples (e.g., Pinchuk’s map) with non‑vanishing Jacobian appear only for higher degrees. Hence the largest integer \(k\) with the property “\(\deg p\le k\) ⇒ \(F\) is globally injective” is  

**\(k=2\).**  

ANSWER: 2
